# University of the Andes (Colombia)
The University of the Andes (Universidad de los Andes or Uniandes) was founded in 1948 by Mario Laserna Pinzón as Colombia's first nonsectarian and politically neutral university, amid a period of political change and economic modernization during the Liberal Republic (1930s-1940s). Its establishment was motivated by a national need for skilled professionals to support rapid industrial growth and social development, and the founders modeled it after the American university system, integrating technical and liberal education. Classes began in 1949 with 80 students, and the university maintained political neutrality during a time of intense violence in Colombia. Early programs included a "three/two" exchange allowing students to complete part of their studies abroad, supported by industrial and philanthropic funding.
Uniandes has since grown into a leading institution offering 14 academic units including 10 faculties and specialized centers. It emphasizes pluralism, academic excellence, and critical ethical formation aligned with social responsibility. Its faculty is predominantly full-time with 70% holding doctorates from top global universities. The student body is highly selective, with 95% admitted from the top 1% of Colombian high school graduates, and around 30% coming from outside Bogotá. The campus blends renovated industrial and religious buildings with modern facilities including numerous classrooms, laboratories, libraries, and sports centers in Bogotá's historical center. The university fosters interdisciplinary study, allowing students to tailor curricula across four academic cycles. It has extensive international exchange programs with over 119 universities worldwide. The mascot is Seneca, a goat symbolizing university tradition. Notable alumni span political leaders, ministers, scientists, artists, and public figures who have contributed significantly to Colombia and beyond.
